text.p: Lehman Brothers said on Sunday Nice Systems Ltd's planned purchase of Canada's Dees Communications was a "major strategic positive" for the Tel Aviv-based company.

Nice said last week it had signed a letter of intent to buy Dees, a provider of automated call centre monitoring solutions, for $8 million in cash and up to 500,000 in ordinary shares. Nice produces digital systems that record and retrieve conversations.
"The acquisition is expected to be non-dilutive to earnings in fiscal 1997 and additive to earnings in 1998," Lehman analyst Tim Luke said in a report.

"We view this as a major strategic positive for Nice Systems...the acquisition of Dees significantly strengthens the company's positioning in the key area of the fast growing U.S. call centre market," Luke said.

Luke said the Dees purchase should immediately triple Nice's U.S. sales force, bring the Israeli firm a new sales channel network, add a strong relationship with Canada's Northern Telecom and includes a call centre consulting group.
Lehman said the acquisition could provide upside to its earnings projections for 1998 and reiterated its 1-Buy rating.

"Our initial price target of $30 is based on our view that over the next 12 months investors are likely to focus on Nice's potential to deliver rapid revenue and earnings growth allowing the shares to trade at a multiple of at least 18 times our 1998 estimate of $1.68," the report said.
Nice is trading on Nasdaq at $26-7/8.
